question: Why is this visarga identified with the principle of desire in the Kula teaching?
premises: The preceding verses established visarga as a surging, wave-like emission.
This emission is unmanifest and has the nature of hakala.
The Kula teaching names this principle kāma-tattva.
inference: The creative emission of visarga is the same reality the Kula tradition calls the principle of desire.
uncertainties: hakala is a technical term whose precise phonetic-cosmic sense is compressed here.
plain_english: For that very reason, O revered secret of the Kula, this visarga—unmanifest and of the nature of hakala—is called the principle of desire.
